title: Volume 1 Chapter 1: The Garden of Women
content: Sitting on a bench in the cargo hold of the transport aircraft, I fastened my seatbelt while wearing my new military uniform. My rank insignia showed that I was a warrant officer. Just six months ago, I had been a corporal, running around the battlefield, and now I had become a candidate for officer status. If my squad leader were here, he would probably salute me with a laugh and tease me. Would MC joke about it if he were alive? He might have been thrilled to have some good material for a comic.

The cargo hold was noisy with the sound of the engines, and I was the only one inside. After enduring the excruciating pain of surgery and rehabilitation, I had finally reached the day when I would be assigned to a base that would serve as the experimental site for the project. I looked at my right hand, gloved in black leather, and clenched it several times to feel the sensation. My left leg was also in decent shape. There was still some discomfort, but it was functioning without any issues. The organs I had lost—especially my heart—were not causing any problems either. My left eye, which had been blind, had regained its sight just as before. It was hard to believe that I had undergone regenerative treatment using cells from a Gijuu, but the agony I experienced during the surgery and rehabilitation was proof enough.
"I'll endure whatever experiments they throw at me and see it through," I muttered to myself just as the pilot's voice crackled through the speakers at full volume.
'We're arriving. Prepare to disembark.'
"Understood," I replied, though I knew my voice wouldn’t reach them. I checked my belongings; I only had a single Boston bag with me.

"Now, I wonder what kind of base this will be," I thought. I had been taken care of at various bases while serving as an infantryman, but bases with stronger units had a reputation for being quite peculiar. I hoped that at a base conducting top-secret experiments, there wouldn't be too many rough characters, but I wouldn't know for sure until I arrived.

When the transport aircraft landed at its destination, I unfastened my seatbelt and stood up. As the rear hatch opened, I walked down the ramp, and waiting for me was Alison Green, the deputy director. She was a woman in a lab coat, just like Dr. Smith, but she had a more sensible appearance. With her blonde hair tied back and green eyes, she looked to be in her forties. I had spoken with her several times over the phone, but this was our first face-to-face meeting.
"Warrant Officer Hifumi Ren reporting!" I saluted, being careful not to misstate my rank, but she looked a bit troubled by my gesture.
"No need for a salute. I'm not military," she said.
"However, I've heard that in this project, you hold the equivalent rank of captain," I replied.
"That's just a title. More importantly, follow me. I'll explain the current situation as we walk," she said, starting to head toward the facility from the arrival area.
I followed Dr. Green as she began to explain the status of the project.

"It's a grandly named project, but finding a suitable location was quite a challenge. With a project of this scale, the necessary facilities are extensive. The options for a host site are limited," she explained.
Considering the scale of the project, it was understandable that the base would bear a significant burden. There was a hint of apology in Dr. Green's tone.
"It will likely be a tough place for you. I apologize in advance," she said.

From her words, it seemed that the base we were about to work with was facing significant issues. However, I had no intention of backing down. To fight against the Gijuu and to prove my worth, I was determined to see this mission through, no matter the circumstances.
"No problem. I'll deliver results in any environment," I assured her.
"Ah, how reassuring. But this time, it might be more difficult than you think," she warned.
"I'm prepared for that," I replied.
"…I see."

As we passed through the aircraft's arrival area, the full scale of the base came into view. I must have widened my eyes in surprise. It seemed I was caught up in a more troublesome situation than I had imagined. Dr. Green turned to me.
"This is the Third Academy, where Valkyries are trained and operated. It seems the academy staff refer to it as Mermaid School," she explained.

I could see the school gates, beyond which stood a large building designed with aesthetics in mind. Inside the academy, girls in uniforms were happily chatting with one another. There was no doubt that this environment was unlike any base I had encountered before. Before I knew it, I had dropped my Boston bag.
Seeing me frozen in place, Dr. Green smiled mischievously, as if pleased with her prank's success.
"It's a harsh environment for a man, isn't it? After all, this is a girls' school," she said.
Caught off guard by a situation I had never anticipated, I remained motionless for a while.

After dropping off my belongings at the dormitory, I was headed to the principal's office. Guided by Dr. Green, I was about to meet the principal of the Third Academy. As I walked behind her, I sought an explanation about the situation.
"Why is there an academy for training Valkyries?" I asked.

Normally, I wouldn’t voice my opinions to a superior, but it seemed I was more unsettled than I realized. Imagining being surrounded by strong soldiers, it was only natural to feel this way when I found myself in an academy filled with younger female students.

Dr. Green answered without turning around. "I already explained this. In this day and age, military bases equipped with such facilities are rare. Plus, the level of confidentiality is top-notch. After all, it's isolated from the outside world."

Looking out the window, I could see the scenery outside the academy. I hadn’t noticed it at the arrival area, but given that this was a Valkyrie academy, it was highly likely that we were in an aerial fortress.
"I had heard rumors about an aerial fortress, but I never thought it actually existed," I admitted.
Rumors of a military base floating in the sky had circulated among infantrymen.
"A fortress, huh? But right now, this is an academy. The principal you’re about to meet is originally in the position of base commander," she clarified.
"Base commander?" I echoed.
"In the organization, she holds the rank of lieutenant general."
A lieutenant general was someone I viewed as being on a different level entirely. However, the idea of a lieutenant general being the principal felt quite strange.

"We've arrived. I don't think it will be a problem, but please don't anger the principal. She was once a Valkyrie and fought as part of the first generation," Dr. Green warned, stopping to give me a serious look, as if recalling something troubling from the past.
I had a single suspicion. "…Did Dr. Smith do something?"
It seemed my guess was correct, as Dr. Green sighed.
"On the first day, he bombarded her with questions and made her angry. —Alison, I've brought the subject you requested," she said, knocking on the door.
"Thank you for waiting," came a voice from inside, which felt distinctly unmilitary.
As the double doors opened, I saw the principal, who was just about to rise from her seat.
"I am Kase Natsuko, the principal of Mermaid School. It's a pleasure to meet you," she greeted with a smile.

At first glance, she appeared to be a graceful woman. While she certainly embodied the term "lady," there was also something unusual about her. Standing taller than me at 180 centimeters, she still had the physique of someone active in the field. The fact that she was dressed in classical Western attire instead of military uniform struck me as particularly odd. Moreover, despite being a lieutenant general, she looked remarkably young. Although I had heard she was of advanced age, the woman before me did not match that description at all.
Hiding my confusion, I saluted and introduced myself.
"Warrant Officer Hifumi Ren reporting for duty. I have been assigned here as of today. I look forward to your guidance."
Principal Kase looked at me with a puzzled smile, tilting her head as she placed a hand on her cheek.
"Hmm, that's a bit stiff. You might stand out here," she remarked, seemingly unimpressed with my greeting.
It appeared that my introduction had not met her expectations. Dr. Green took over and continued the conversation.
"He is in a special position. Generally, he will need permission to leave the facilities we are borrowing, so we will make efforts to minimize contact with the female students."

The Valkyries were all young women who could easily be attending school. It was best to avoid contact with someone like me, Dr. Green suggested. I completely agreed, but Principal Kase didn’t seem satisfied, wearing a troubled expression.
"Then that would defeat the purpose of accepting him. The reason I accepted the Prometheus Project was for the sake of the children," she insisted.
"Children? You mean the female students?" I wondered.
When I glanced at Dr. Green, I noticed a slight furrow in her brow. It seemed her reaction was not merely due to the unexpected situation.
Quickly regaining her composure, I sought to understand Principal Kase's true intentions.
"I thought we had agreed to minimize contact?" I asked.
Principal Kase smiled, but there was an undeniable pressure in her demeanor.

"Yes, I want you to interact minimally. No inappropriate relationships, of course. However, in a girls' school, opportunities to learn about relationships with the opposite sex are limited, right? I want the female students to learn a bit about how to interact with boys," she explained.
Was this a concern of hers as an educator? Dr. Green wore a troubled expression at Principal Kase's wishes, but it seemed she was willing to accept them.
"Understood. We'll finalize the details later," Dr. Green said.
"Thank you. Oh, and one more thing," Principal Kase said, stepping closer to me.
As she approached, wearing heels, she looked down at me.
"Not many will welcome you here, so keep that in mind. As principal, I will keep an eye on things, but my students can be a bit rough, so be careful," she warned.
"…Thank you for the advice," I replied.

After leaving the principal's office, Dr. Green's stride was wider than when we had entered. Her back seemed to show signs of irritation regarding Principal Kase's earlier attitude as she hurried toward the development team's hangar.
"It seems this project is not even on her radar," she said.
"Is that so?" I asked.

"Did you not notice? If a man successfully becomes a combat asset against the Gijuu, it will be the Valkyries who feel the repercussions. The budget distribution within the organization will change, and their political standing will be jeopardized. To think the reason she accepted us was to teach the female students about relationships with boys… she really underestimates us," Dr. Green explained.

If a man succeeded in becoming a combat asset, it would mark the end of the Valkyries' dominance. This tied back to what Principal Kase had said about not welcoming me. I was seen as an obstacle or even an enemy to this academy.
However, I had more pressing personal issues to deal with right now.
"…Dr. Green," I began.
"Just call me Alison," she replied.
"Then I have a question for you, Alison," I said.
"What is it?"
As I followed her, I sought answers regarding the issues that had arisen earlier.
"I haven't received any training on how to interact with women. How should I approach them? If there are any textbooks, I would like to borrow one," I inquired.
Since being sent to the facility, I had had very few opportunities to interact with women. I had no experience in dealing with female students. How was I supposed to tackle this difficult situation?
Alison stopped and turned her upper body to look at me, her eyes wide in surprise.
"Are you serious?" she asked.
"Yes," I confirmed.
I realized I was woefully unprepared for this issue. Placing a hand on her forehead, Alison let out a deep sigh. It seemed I had disappointed her by revealing my lack of training.
"I didn't expect you to be a problem child too," she said.
"Did you hear? A guy is transferring in," two students were discussing in the hallway of the school.
"Isn't it about that experiment? I don't understand what the principal is thinking, accepting someone who will probably fail," one of them said.
Louise Duran, a student wearing a gray blazer over a white shirt, stopped and interrupted their conversation with a curious expression.
"What are you talking about?"

With a gentle demeanor, Louise had long silver hair that was loosely styled and a warm, friendly aura. Her yellow, droopy eyes and laid-back tone made her well-liked among her classmates in Class Five.
The two students welcomed her into the conversation without hesitation.
"You heard, right? A male pilot is coming to this academy. There's a rumor that he might transfer into our Class Five," one of them explained.
"Though it's practically a done deal," the other added.

While there were male staff members at the academy, they were rarely seen in the classrooms or dormitories where the female students lived. The idea of a male entering their Class Five seemed to unsettle the two girls.
Louise smiled, looking a bit troubled.
"…That's the first I've heard of it," she admitted.
The two girls exchanged exasperated glances at Louise's ignorance.
"You really are out of the loop when it comes to trends and rumors, Louise. Well, that's the situation; a boy is going to be our classmate," one of them said.
When one mentioned the boy, the other burst into laughter.
"A boy? From what I heard about the kid I saw by chance, he looks like he's over twenty. He's definitely not a boy," she scoffed.
When they said he wasn't a boy, Louise placed her hands on her hips and puffed out her chest.
"That's not wrong. The character for 'child' is made up of 'one' and 'finished,' meaning from beginning to end, so I think it's fine to call him a boy," she argued.

Louise had come to Japan before entering middle school due to her parents' circumstances and had passed the Valkyrie aptitude test to enroll in the Third Academy. Although her Japanese had been poor at first, she was diligent and had kept up with her language studies.
As she proudly showcased her learned words, the two girls exchanged amused glances.
"It might not be wrong, but it's not how people generally refer to it," one pointed out.
"There are words like that, but it sounds just like you, Louise," the other added.
Her classmates seemed to view Louise as somewhat scatterbrained.
Feeling embarrassed, Louise blushed.
"N-No way? Ugh, I messed up again! I bragged about it to so many people!"
As the two girls comforted a saddened Louise, a group of girls wearing capes over their uniforms approached.
One girl, wearing a gray cape, had a quiet appearance with black bobbed hair and glasses. The girl walking behind her had medium-length hair and wore a red cape.
Noticing the three, the black-haired girl seemed indifferent, but the red-caped girl stopped right in front of Louise and her friends, glaring at them with sharp eyes.
Louise, caught in the gaze, forced a smile.
"Long time no see… Hayase-san," she said.

The girl was Hayase Maya, a former classmate from middle school who had now risen to a higher status than Louise. The cape she wore was a mark of a fully-fledged Valkyrie. Among those with colored capes, she was considered a special presence.
For the girls in Class Five, those allowed to wear capes were seen as superior.
"You seem the same as ever… I don't like it," Maya said, stating her feelings before losing interest and chasing after the black-haired girl who had moved on.
Once they left, Louise let out a sigh of relief.
"Phew, that was scary," she said.
Her classmates immediately turned to her for clarification.
"Hey, why was Hayase glaring at you?" one asked.
"You're classmates, right? Did something happen?" the other pressed.
With a sheepish smile, Louise scratched her cheek.
"I've been disliked by her since middle school. I don't hate her, but it seems Hayase-san… dislikes me," she explained.
Her classmates looked at her with sympathetic eyes.
"To think a classmate who hated you back then is now an ace… and of all people, that Hayase. How unfortunate," one said.
"Being disliked by the strongest Valkyrie in the academy, Louise, that's rough," the other added.

Being disliked by an ace was a significant disadvantage for the girls in Class Five, who were treated as reserve forces. Moreover, within the context of individual skill, Maya was reputed to be the strongest at the Third Academy.

In fact, even the teachers regarded Maya as exceptional. Her only flaw was her tendency to isolate herself, making it difficult for her to connect with others. She fought alone on the battlefield, earning her the nickname "the lone warrior" among her peers.
As her classmates looked at Louise with pity, they couldn't help but tease her.
"It seems your school life is already over," one joked.
Louise's face turned sorrowful.
"Don't say that! I know this situation isn't good for me either!"
As Maya caught up to the girl ahead of her, Sorajima Mai, she was questioned about her earlier actions.
Mai kept her gaze forward, not even turning to look at her.
"Why were you intimidating those girls from Class Five? That's not like you," she remarked.
Maya maintained a disgruntled expression.
"There was a girl I disliked since middle school," she replied.
"The silver-haired girl? I heard she was on the scout list from Miou-sensei… Did you refuse to work with her?" Mai asked, turning her head slightly to glance at Maya.
Her sharp gaze seemed to harbor anger toward Maya's selfishness.
"I simply answered when asked. I told them I didn't want to fight alongside that girl," Maya said dismissively.
"That's a sufficient reason for an ace to refuse. It seems you don't understand the situation in Class Three, do you?" Mai pressed.
"I understand," Maya replied curtly, clearly unwilling to continue the conversation.
But Mai was relentless.

"She's talented. I've heard other classes are interested in her, and we can't afford to delay reinforcements for Class Three because of your selfishness. —You need to be more aware of your role as an ace."
As Mai faced forward, Maya's displeasure grew.
"No one asked me to be an ace," she shot back.

"Only four people in this academy can wear colored capes. Since you've been chosen as one of them, don't you think you should be aware of your position? —The strongest and most solitary female warrior," Mai challenged.
While Maya was the strongest as an individual, her solitary fighting style meant she fell short in group battles.
Provoked by Mai's teasing smile, Maya retorted, "The words of a former ace carry a different weight, don't they? Just because you lost your position to me doesn't mean you can take it out on me."
When Mai stopped, Maya did too.
The atmosphere grew tense, but Mai only turned her upper body slightly.
Her expression seemed sad.
"You have talent, but you're selfish and willful—you're suited to be an ace. I question your character, but I hope you continue to do your best for Class Three," she said.
Maya, taken aback by the response, shot back at her superior.
"I have no interest in classes. I fight only for myself."
Her words were not a facade; Maya was speaking her true feelings.
There was no shame in fighting for oneself.
Mai let out a small sigh.
"Do as you please. As long as it benefits Class Three, I won't concern myself with your personality."
